memory_leads.lead: Qualified-seafarer supply is a multi-stage production pipeline rather than a stock of certificate holders. Prospective entrants/cadets, education and training providers, shipowners or shipmanagers supplying sea-time berths, assessors/examiners and administrations controlling certification or endorsements form distinct capacity gates.

Entry and cadet selection determine the pipeline's future cohort before any licensed labor appears. Sponsorship, prerequisites, aptitude or medical/document readiness and willingness to pursue a sea career can constrain intake; exact selection systems and demographics require Evidence.

Education and practical preparation are different states. Classroom/theory learning, workshop or laboratory practice, simulator exposure and supervised practical exercises build different components of competence and do not substitute perfectly for experience aboard an operating ship.

Access to an approved or otherwise qualifying sea-service berth can be the bottleneck between training and certification. A person can complete shore education yet remain unable to advance because the industry supplies too few suitable onboard training places or because berth timing does not match the learner's progression.

Sea time is not merely elapsed calendar time: supervised task exposure, vessel/trade context and recorded experience can matter to readiness even when exact regulatory credit rules are deferred. Nominal time served therefore need not equal practical competence.

Assessment and examination are separate gates from course completion. A candidate may be training-complete but awaiting assessment, may fail and require remediation, or may pass while still awaiting administrative issuance; these states create queues before labor becomes deployable.

Certification and endorsement are eligibility states rather than proof of vessel-specific operational readiness. A document can establish formal qualification for a role while P032 familiarization, recent practice and company/vessel procedures still determine how quickly the person becomes effective onboard.

Recognition or endorsement across administrations can affect portability of qualified labor between fleets. The structural state is whether a credential is accepted for the intended assignment; exact recognition arrangements, flags and certificate forms require Evidence.

Promotion creates a rank pipeline with long lags. Moving from junior to senior roles typically requires accumulated experience, qualifying service, assessment and demonstrated competence, so a shortage of senior officers cannot be repaired instantly by recruiting more entry-level cadets.

Specialized vessel, cargo, machinery or operating roles can add qualification layers on top of general rank competence. A labor pool may therefore look ample in aggregate while the subset eligible and familiar for a particular ship type or technology remains scarce.

Continuing competence is a lifecycle after initial certification: recurrent training, refresher activity, practice, revalidation or adaptation to changed equipment/procedures can affect deployability and readiness. Exact intervals and mandatory content require Evidence.

Training capacity has throughput and lead-time constraints. Instructor/assessor availability, simulator or workshop slots, school capacity and onboard berths can create queues whose effects appear years later in rank-specific labor supply rather than immediately in fleet statistics.

Career attrition acts at every stage: entrants may leave training, qualified junior staff may leave seagoing work, and experienced officers may move ashore or exit the industry. The resulting senior-rank supply is a survivor pipeline, not simply prior intake minus retirements.

P032 competency/familiarization is refined by separating formal eligibility, assessed competence, recent practice and vessel-specific familiarity. These states should not be collapsed into a single qualified/not-qualified flag.

P033 recruitment and joining are downstream of a slower qualification pipeline. An employer can have strong recruiting reach yet still face shortages if the required rank, specialization or endorsement cannot be produced quickly enough.

P034 bargaining and wage pressure can be shaped by pipeline elasticity: labor terms may react differently to a temporary joining bottleneck versus a multi-year shortage of experienced or specialized personnel whose supply requires promotion and sea-time accumulation.

Known-time replay should distinguish expected graduation, completed training, accrued qualifying service, assessment outcome, certificate/endorsement issuance and actual first deployable assignment. Later certification cannot be backfilled into an earlier period when availability was still uncertain.

P032 already established that general competence and vessel-specific familiarization differ; P035 locates that distinction within the upstream qualification pipeline rather than repeating the operating-state claim.
The atlas already notes labor/crewing under-recall and effective capacity constraints; P035 supplies the formation mechanism for qualified labor rather than repeating those broad themes.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: Exact content, required service, exams, certificate classes and regulatory changes vary by role, administration and period and require dated Evidence.
Provider history, capacity, quality and outcomes would become a salience-biased directory without source-first research.
Credential recognition and validity are jurisdiction- and date-specific legal/administrative facts requiring Evidence.
Current 2025-2026 pipeline conditions and shortage claims require fresh source-first collection rather than blind memory.

stop_reason: The qualified-seafarer formation pipeline is populated from entry/cadet selection through shore and practical training, sea-service berth access, assessment, certification/endorsement, familiarization, promotion and continuing competence. Further recall becomes standard-, course-, certificate-, school-, pass-rate-, examiner-, company- or jurisdiction-specific.
truth_boundary: Memory-only orientation; no training standard, course quality, qualifying sea-time, certificate validity, endorsement recognition, exam outcome, school performance, rank shortage or current labor-supply condition is verified.
